concept: MongoDB Search searchNodePreference routing and result consistency

claims.text: SERVER-124090, updated October 23, 2026, is an unresolved improvement with no fix version. It specifies x-mongodb-searchnodepreference as xxHash64(searchNodePreference.key), alongside command and shard headers, and requests equivalent metadata for legacy aggregate, planShardedSearch, and search-cursor getMore paths. This describes engineering requirements for fallback routing, not proof that a particular released version implements them. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Affinity improves potential result consistency without guaranteeing permanent consistency. MongoDB explicitly lists changes in the dataset, index structure, cluster topology, and preferred-node availability as causes of remaining inconsistencies. Treating the key as a frozen result snapshot would exceed the documented guarantee. (high confidence)

A practical consequence of the documented affinity contract is to reuse the same preference key for a sequence of related requests when repeatability matters. Changing the key removes that sequence's stated same-value routing condition; keeping it still does not freeze the underlying results. This is application guidance inferred from the contract. (medium confidence)

Percona's October 1, 2026 $vectorSearch reference includes searchNodePreference: {key: <preference-string>} in its syntax, but its field table does not explain affinity semantics. It corroborates the parameter shape in a separate implementation context, not Atlas availability, failure behavior, or consistency guarantees. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)

Routing affinity does not remove the usual result-fetching stage: mongot returns matching document IDs and metadata, and mongod normally looks up the documents. The separate returnStoredSource option controls returning stored fields instead of the backend document lookup. (high confidence)

The $search stage accepts the optional object searchNodePreference: {key: <arbitrary string>}. Keeping the key value unchanged preferentially routes repeated queries to the same search node and overrides default search-node routing. (high confidence)

With separate mongod and mongot nodes, read preference first selects mongod. By default mongod sends the search through its local load balancer across mongot processes; searchNodePreference changes search-node routing at this second step. These are distinct routing controls. (high confidence)

The related $vectorSearch syntax also includes searchNodePreference with a key string in both MongoDB and Percona documentation. Percona documents its own product syntax; this does not independently establish Atlas routing or result-consistency behavior. (medium confidence)
